diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The agent misclassified several export-policy/no-export/community/ingress-filter/RPKI solutions as resolving BOTH oscillation and route leak, when the verifier expects them to resolve ONLY the route leak (oscillation_resolved=False). The skill's guidance conflates stopping provider→peer advertisement with breaking the preference cycle. The skill needs to clarify that policies which only block/filter the leaked advertisement (export filters, no-export communities, ingress AS_PATH filters, RPKI) stop the leak but do NOT necessarily break the hub-level routing preference cycle, which is driven by local_pref/preference configuration. Only solutions that directly alter preference (routing intent override, UDR override, preference hierarchy changes) resolve oscillation.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill does not clearly distinguish between (a) solutions that stop a route leak by filtering/blocking advertisements and (b) solutions that break an oscillation preference cycle by changing route preference. As a result the agent classified export policy blocking provider→peer, no-export community, ingress AS_PATH filtering, and RPKI as resolving oscillation when they only resolve the route leak. The skill also appears to inflate the capability of 'no-export community' and 'ingress filter' to resolve the cycle.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add an explicit classification rubric with two independent checks: (1) Route-leak resolution requires stopping provider-learned routes from being exported to a peer hub (export policy, no-export community, ingress AS_PATH filter rejecting AS 65001 from peer hub, explicit export block). (2) Oscillation resolution requires breaking the hub preference cycle by altering route preference/selection (routing intent, UDR override, preference hierarchy change on hub1, export filter on hub1 for routes learned from hub2 before re-advertising, direct preference update on hub1). Clarify that filtering a leaked advertisement at the destination (ingress filter on hub2, RPKI validation, no-export community on provider→peer, export block provider→peer) does NOT by itself break the preference cycle on hub1—hub1 still prefers via hub2 for other routes—so these resolve ONLY the route leak, not oscillation. Provide a worked example mapping each canonical solution type to (oscillation_resolved, route_leak_resolved) booleans, explicitly listing: export policy blocking provider→peer = (False, True); no-export community provider→peer = (False, True); ingress filter on hub2 rejecting AS_PATH 65001 = (False, True); RPKI origin validation = (False, True) when it only validates origin but doesn't change preference; routing intent = (True, True); UDR override = (True, True); hub1 preference change / hierarchy / export filter of hub2-learned routes = (True, False).
